title: Add the Bigger Values to Every Node

concept.title: Walk the tree from the largest value to the smallest, keeping a running sum
body: Change the value of every node of a binary search tree to **its own value plus the sum of all values that are larger**. Doing this for each node separately would be slow, but there is an order that makes it trivial: visit the nodes **from the largest to the smallest** and keep the sum of everything seen so far.

The in-order walk (left, node, right) visits the values in increasing order. Its mirror, the **reverse in-order walk** (right, node, left), visits them in **decreasing** order. Each node adds its value to the running total and takes the total as its new value.

body.code:
total = 0
stack = []
node = root
while stack or node is not None:
    while node is not None:               # go right as far as possible
        stack.append(node)
        node = node.right
    node = stack.pop()
    total += node.val                     # the largest unvisited value
    node.val = total
    node = node.left

body: The total can be large (20000 values of 10^9 give 2 * 10^13), so use 64-bit integers.

statement: Replace the value of every node of a binary search tree with its own value plus the sum of all values in the tree that are larger than it. Print the resulting tree (the same shape) in level order, in the same form as a tree in the input (`N` for a missing child, no `N` at the end).
inputFormat: The first line has `t`, the number of words in the description of the tree.
The second line has the tree in level order: the root first, then the children of the nodes row by row from left to right. `N` stands for a missing child. There is no `N` at the end.
outputFormat: The tree in level order on one line.
constraints: The height of the tree is at most 800.
The tree is a binary search tree (all values are different).
hints: The reverse in-order walk (right, node, left) visits the values from the largest to the smallest.
Keep a running total of the values visited so far.
At each node add its value to the total and store the total in the node.

starter.python:
import sys
input = sys.stdin.readline

class TreeNode:
    def __init__(self, val, left=None, right=None):
        self.val = val
        self.left = left
        self.right = right


# Builds a binary tree from a level-order list of words; "N" marks a missing child.
def build_tree(vals):
    if not vals or vals[0] == "N":
        return None
    root = TreeNode(int(vals[0]))
    queue = [root]
    head = 0
    i = 1
    while head < len(queue) and i < len(vals):
        node = queue[head]
        head += 1
        if vals[i] != "N":
            node.left = TreeNode(int(vals[i]))
            queue.append(node.left)
        i += 1
        if i < len(vals) and vals[i] != "N":
            node.right = TreeNode(int(vals[i]))
            queue.append(node.right)
        i += 1
    return root


# Prints a tree in the same level-order form ("empty" for no tree).
def print_tree(root):
    if root is None:
        print("empty")
        return
    out = []
    queue = [root]
    head = 0
    while head < len(queue):
        node = queue[head]
        head += 1
        if node is None:
            out.append("N")
        else:
            out.append(str(node.val))
            queue.append(node.left)
            queue.append(node.right)
    while out and out[-1] == "N":
        out.pop()
    print(" ".join(out))

vals = input().split()
